title: Remove the Mac and tablet runtime wording the owner sees
requested_outcome: CLIVE now runs on a Linux server and the owner uses an iPhone, but owner-facing text still speaks of a Mac and a tablet, for example 'The Mac is still reading recent orders, so this is what it holds so far.' (app/fastpath/library.py), 'Cannot reach the assistant. Is the Mac awake and is it running (make up)?', 'generated on the Mac', 'the Mac unreachable' (web/app.js), 'The Mac answered <status>.' (web/alpha.js), 'Not from the Mac itself' (web/action-state.js), and the login messages in app/providers/max_agent_sdk.py ('needs a logged-in Mac', 'My Claude login is not working on the Mac'). Find every string the owner can see or hear that names the Mac, a tablet, launchd or 'make up' as the runtime, and rewrite it in plain, host-neutral words that stay true on any host (CLIVE, the server, this device), without changing behaviour. Code comments may stay. If a test pins one of these strings, update that expectation to the new wording and change nothing else in it. Add a test that scans the owner-facing string sources for these runtime words so they cannot return. The previous attempt (branch clive/objective/owner-facing-host-wording-2 in this repository) was blocked because the spoken refusals are defined in app/routes/actions.py (SPOKEN_REFUSALS) and used in app/routes/turn.py; both are now in scope for their owner-facing wording only. Reuse that attempt where it is sound. Run every check listed below in your workspace and fix anything it reports before you report. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically after your candidate is published.
acceptance_criteria: no owner-facing string names the Mac, a tablet, launchd or make up as the runtime
behaviour is unchanged apart from wording
a test guards against the runtime words returning
every listed check passes in the worker's workspace
